Monoclonal antisera are produced from a single clone of B cells, meaning all antibodies are identical and recognize the same epitope on an antigen. Polyclonal antisera come from multiple B cell clones, producing a mixture of antibodies that recognize different epitopes, possibly on the same or related antigens.  

Option (C) correctly captures this distinction: monoclonal antibodies come from descendants of a single B lymphocyte, while polyclonal antibodies come from descendants of different B lymphocytes.  

Final answer: (C)
